title.title: Strong cosmic censorship near two-ended Kerr data
title.subtitle: Claim: near each fixed rotating Kerr, data with a square-integrable-connection extension are non-generic

object.axisLabel: regularity asked of a future extension, weaker to stronger

beats.text: Can a black-hole interior be continued past its Cauchy horizon? It depends on regularity
Near Kerr, continuous extensions exist: the $C^0$ form of censorship is false
Claim: extensions with square-integrable connection form a meagre set

achievement.label: Strong cosmic censorship, Christodoulou's formulation
statement: \{\text{data near Kerr with a } C^0 \cap W^{1,2}_{\rm loc} \text{ extension}\}
achievement.context: Before: no near-Kerr genericity result without symmetry; Luk–Oh had spherical symmetry
achievement.note: Local only: a small neighbourhood of each fixed Kerr with $0 < |a| < M$

verify.detail: No formalization; about 278 pages across three mutually dependent papers
verify.ourCheck: We read the papers' claims and caveats; we did not referee them

sources.quote: ~278 pages across three mutually dependent papers
Dafermos-Luk proved C^0 stability of the Kerr Cauchy horizon (arXiv:1710.01722), so the C^0 formulation is false near Kerr

plain: Can spacetime be continued past the inside of a black hole? For typical ones, not smoothly enough to matter

steps: Suppose the interior could be continued smoothly enough
Then tiny loops force one curvature measure to be small
A late gravitational wave makes it large: typical data can't

voice.text: Continuous extensions past the horizon exist. The question is whether smoother ones do.
If one existed, tiny loops force curvature small; a late wave makes it large.
Claimed: typical nearby data allow none.
